properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued October 23 at 2:56AM MDT until October 23 at 6:00PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Big Rock burn scar and Ohio burn
scar.

following areas, in central Idaho, Wood River Foothills. In
southeast Idaho, Upper Snake River Plain.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar is
expected up to and during the period of the watch. Residents near
the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar should prepare for potential debris
flow. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding and debris
flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Big Rock and Ohio burn scar, which may lead to
flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Heise.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, strong
gusty winds, and a wind shift with a cold front will create
erratic fire behavior and difficult control of new or existing
fires.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In North Central WY Fire Zone...274.
In Southeast MT Fire Zone...131.
In Southeast MT and Northwest SD Fire Zone...133.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In North Central WY...Sheridan.
In Northwest SD...Harding.
In South Central MT...Big Horn.
In Southeast MT...Carter...Fallon...Powder River...Rosebud
Treasure.

The most dangerous conditions are expected along and southeast of
a Baker Montana to Sheridan Wyoming line.

* COLD FRONT: Late afternoon into early evening.

* WIND: Southwest 20 to 30 mph gusting up to 45 mph. Winds shifting
to the northwest behind a late day cold front, with continued
gusts to 45 mph through much of tonight.

* HUMIDITY: Minimums of 14 to 20 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Highs of 75 to 85 degrees.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong
winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute
to extreme fire behavior.

* WHAT...For the Hazardous Seas Warning, very steep and hazardous
seas 9 to 13 ft at 10 seconds and north winds 15 to 25 kt with
gusts up to 30 kt. For the Small Craft Advisory, seas 7 to 9 ft
at 11 seconds and north winds 10 to 20 kt with gusts up to 25
kt expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Waters from Cape Shoalwater to Florence out 60
NM.

* WHEN...Hazardous Seas Warning, until 8 AM PDT this morning.
Small Craft Advisory, from 8 AM this morning to 5 PM PDT this
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Very steep and hazardous seas could capsize or cause
damage to vessels.
properties.instruction:
A Hazardous Seas Warning means hazardous sea conditions are
imminent or occurring. Recreational boaters should remain in
port, or take shelter until waves subside.  Commercial vessels
should prepare for rough seas and consider remaining in port or
taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

properties.areaDesc: Monroe Lower Keys
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued October 23 at 4:00AM EDT until October 24 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Lower Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and
lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD STATEMENT REMAINS IN EFFECT

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 4:00AM EDT until October 24 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Upper and Middle Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Until 5 AM EDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater flooding of low elevation streets and lots
is expected. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Montezuma, CO
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 23 at 1:51AM MDT until October 23 at 1:45PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Montezuma County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 145 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 150 AM MDT, Gauge reports indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dolores River and Lost Canyon Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dolores.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 145 PM MDT THIS AFTERNOON

properties.areaDesc: La Plata, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 1:47AM MDT until October 23 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding with road washouts also occurring.
Streams and dry washes continue to rise due to excess runoff from
earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 147 AM MDT, local law enforcement reported flooding in the
warned area. Flooding is already occurring. Between 1.5 and 2
inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes but is not limited to the following streams
anddrainages...
Florida River, Spring Creek, Ute Creek, Salt Creek and Dry Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Bayfield, Ignacio, Oxford, Tiffany and Allison.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.headline: Dense Fog Advisory issued October 23 at 3:46AM EDT until October 23 at 10:00AM EDT by NWS Marquette MI
properties.description:
* WHAT...Visibility 1/4 mile or less in dense fog.

* WHERE...Portions of central Upper and western Upper Michigan.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM EDT /9 AM CDT/ this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas along the Lake Superior shoreline can
expect less in the way of fog due to light, southerly downslope
flow. Be prepared for rapidly changing conditions if you are headed
inland.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.areaDesc: Archuleta, CO; Hinsdale, CO; La Plata, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 1:46AM MDT until October 23 at 4:00AM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Western Archuleta County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern Hinsdale County in southwestern Colorado...
Southern La Plata County in southwestern Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 400 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 146 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
La Plata River, Animas River, Vallecito Creek, Taylor Creek, Los
Pinos River, Florida River, and First Fork Piedra River.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Durango, La Plata, Falfa, Hesperus, Bondad, Breen, Mayday, Kline,
Marvel, Redmesa and Vallecito.
- Flooding along the Animas River, including areas on the north
side of Durango, is ongoing or expected to begin shortly. Rivers
and streams will continue to rise through the night, with peak
flow expected Friday afternoon.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 4 AM MDT EARLY THIS MORNING

* WHERE...Lancaster and Lebanon Counties.

plumbing.
